findings.finding: FR-presence used truthiness. FIXED: is_non_empty_fr_list.
closed-code rule was opt-in via intent. FIXED: intent stamped from the iterate entry type, mismatch refused.
remote-first rule fell through to local main; missing git read as not-a-repo; ls-files without --full-name lost untracked files in a subdirectory project. FIXED, real-git tests.
monorepo docs covered runtime prompts; generic **/docs globs covered runtime trees; shape read from the working tree. FIXED.
reason code never compared with change_type; no compliance-only code. FIXED.
stale docs, F11 drift, dead re-export, test names. FIXED.
Claim under doubt: untracked files are part of the diff — ls-files without --full-name drops them for a project in a repo subdirectory
Claim under doubt: generic projects keep runtime code outside every label — src/app/docs/page.tsx passes under docs
findings.suggestion: FIXED (runtime roots win over docs/test/sbom globs).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a no-FR label cannot cover a requirement change — .shipwright/** is bookkeeping for every label, so a docs label can edit spec.md
findings.suggestion: ACCEPTED limit in the ADR; follow-up: exclude planning spec files from bookkeeping.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the label is checked against what the iterate changed — checked once at F5b; the idempotent early return in finalize_iterate skips the gate on re-run; a stale plugin cache bypasses it
findings.suggestion: ACCEPTED limits 5-6 in the ADR; F11 WARNs on a none event without a closed code.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: stacked campaign branches measure only this unit — fork point is always trunk
findings.suggestion: ACCEPTED limit (fails closed, names the paths).

findings.finding: The `none` branch runs before the FR check and is unconditional: any event recording `spec_impact: "none"` must supply a justification and a reason code even when `affected_frs`/`new_frs` are present. The spec text ("one that names no requirement and gives no reason is rejected") and the new F5b.md / F7.md docs ("A feature, change or bug with no affected_frs/new_frs must set spec_impact none + justification + code") both scope the requirement to the no-FR case. The code is stricter than both. The diff itself shows this combination was common in practice — `test_fr_gate_test_evidence.py` and `test_finalize_test_evidence_gate.py` events had `spec_impact: none` + `affected_frs` with no justification and had to be patched to keep passing.
findings.suggestion: Either gate the `none` branch on `not (affected_frs or new_frs)` to match the documented contract, or update F5b.md/F7.md/spec AC03 to say the justification+code is required for every `spec_impact: none`. As written, code and docs disagree, and legitimate docs-only FR-linked iterates get refused.

findings.finding: If a `rev-list --count` call fails (non-zero return, empty stdout) for one of the trunk pairs, the comparison silently reads as "not an ancestor," so two trunk refs that are ordered can be reported as "share no ordering" and the write is refused (`change_type_diff_unavailable`). Fail-closed, so not a bypass, but a transient git fault turns into a hard refusal with a misleading repair message.
findings.suggestion: Check `returncode != 0` on the `rev-list` calls and raise a `DiffUnavailable` with the actual stderr instead of the "no ordering" message.

findings.finding: docs/` is anchored at the root, so a nested `packages/foo/docs/` directory in a generic-shaped repo is not covered by the `docs` label (only `/.md` is). A pure-documentation change under `packages/foo/docs/` that also touches, e.g., `packages/foo/docs/requirements.txt` would be refused with no available label. Narrow but real for pnpm/Lerna-style layouts, which the WebUI-shape tests don't cover.
findings.suggestion: Add `/docs/` to `_DOCS` (it can't widen anything dangerous — it only covers markdown-ish trees), or document the limitation.

findings.finding: The collector-crash test monkeypatches `drift_parsers.collect_requirements_from_planning`, but the fail-closed behavior depends on `specs_found` being flipped to `True` before the patched call inside `collect_known_fr_ids` — code that is not visible in the diff (only the `specs_found = False` init and the final `except` are shown). If the ordering in the hidden body ever changes (e.g., the flag is set after collection succeeds), this test still passes via the re-imported patched symbol but the production guarantee silently inverts.
findings.suggestion: Also assert the positive path explicitly — a repo with a parseable spec returning a non-empty id set with `specs_found=True` — to pin the flag's set point.

findings.finding: Allowing `/.mdx` as documentation lets executable WebUI pages bypass FR linkage. For example, changing `src/app/page.mdx` can alter rendered product behavior while passing the `docs` exemption. The tests only check runtime files with `.tsx`, `.ts`, and `.py` extensions.
findings.suggestion: Classify MDX under runtime page directories as runtime code, even when its extension resembles documentation. Add a WebUI test showing that a docs-only event changing such a page is refused.

findings.finding: Coercing the justification through `str()` accepts JSON booleans, numbers, lists, and objects as explanations. An FR-linked F5b event with `spec_impact: "none"`, `spec_impact_justification: true`, and a valid reason code passes without the required one-line textual justification; multiline strings also pass.
findings.suggestion: Require a non-empty string with no line breaks before accepting the justification. Test malformed values through F5b as well as the shared gate.  Ship-with-fixes: the shared enforcement addresses the main bypasses, but these gaps still admit invalid exemptions or records. Repository access was blocked, so this assessment is limited to the supplied specification and diff; the referenced BRIEF and tests could not be independently checked.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
